title: Multithreaded Monte Carlo option pricing
summary: Price a European call by simulation, check it against Black–Scholes, then parallelise it three ways: per-thread partial sums, a mutex-protected total and an atomic total. TSan checks every version.

steps.title: Sequential pricer
hints: `std::mt19937_64 rng{ seed };` then `payoff_sum(p, paths, rng)` (given in `mc_core.hpp`).
Discount the average payoff: `exp(-r·T) · sum / paths`.

steps.title: One RNG and one slot per thread
hints: Never share an RNG between threads: give thread `t` its own `std::mt19937_64 rng{ seed + t }`.
Split the paths as evenly as possible; each thread writes `partial[t]` only.

steps.title: Mutex vs atomic accumulation
hints: Mutex: compute a batch's sum without the lock, then lock only for `total += s`.
`std::atomic<double>` has no portable `+=` before C++20. Use `compare_exchange_weak` in a loop.
Locking once per path would serialise everything: batch the updates.
